item.title: Goldman Sachs Sells Eternal Shares Via A ₹169 Cr Block Deal
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Financial service giant Goldman Sachs has sold 53.4 Lakh shares of foodtech giant Eternal in a major block deal worth…
item.content:encoded:
Financial service giant Goldman Sachs has sold 53.4 Lakh shares of foodtech giant Eternal in a major block deal worth ₹168.7 Cr.

According to NSE data, the investment bank, via its entity Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, sold the shares at ₹316 apiece to rake in the amount. The investor offloaded the stake at a discount of more than 2.6% to the stock’s last closing price on Thursday. 

The shares that flooded the market were lapped up by Bank of America, via its affiliate BofA Securities Europe, for ₹168.7 Cr.

This is the second block witnessed by Eternal in the past two months. In early September, French financial services giant BNP Paribas and US-based hedge fund Millennium Management together sold over 9.9 Cr shares of the listed foodtech giant for a sum of ₹3,264.8 Cr.

This latest block deal comes as investors continue to be bullish on Eternal. Shares of the foodtech giant have surged nearly 10% in the past three months, and are up 16.2% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis.

The uptick in Eternal’s shares has come on the back of strong financial performance by the startup despite intensifying competition in the quick commerce space and the entry of new players like Rapido’s Ownly, Flipkart and Swish. What has been powering the stock’s rise is Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit, which continues to dominate the instant delivery market.

On the financial front, Eternal reported a consolidated net profit of ₹92 Cr in Q1 FY27, up nearly 3.7X from ₹25 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, operating revenue surged 182% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹20,211 Cr during the quarter under review. 

Shares of Eternal closed Thursday’s trading session 2.77% higher at ₹324.35 on the BSE.

item.title: Inside SEBI’s 10 Key Proposed Changes To SME IPO Rules
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed sweeping changes to the rules governing initial public offerings (IPOs)…
item.content:encoded:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed sweeping changes to the rules governing initial public offerings (IPOs) of small and medium enterprises (SMEs). 

In a consultation paper floated on October 14, the markets regulator has proposed changes to SME IPO norms, including regulations pertaining to valuation thresholds, profitability and shareholder exits. The regulator has invited public feedback on the paper till November 4. 

Citing its rationale, the regulator said that the paper has been formulated by its working group due to rapid increase in the funds raised through SME IPOs and the number of investors participating in such issues. 

Since launch in 2012, about 1,500 companies have opted to list on the SME platform and have raised ₹40,222 Cr. Startups like Zappfresh, DroneAcharya, TAC Infosec, Yudiz, are a few startups that have also taken this route to go public.

In view of this, the regulator has proposed multiple changes, including lowering the minimum application threshold and removing mandatory underwriting and market-making requirements.

Here’s a look at some of the key changes that have been proposed:

The Market Cap-Based Listing Criteria

Under the proposed framework, companies with a post-issue market capitalisation of ₹1,000 Cr or less can now list on the SME platform. Those valued in the range of ₹1,000 Cr to ₹4,000 Cr can also choose to list either on the SME platform or the main board. Companies valued over ₹4,000 Cr will have to list on the main board.

SEBI has also proposed replacing the existing paid-up share capital criterion with post-issue market capitalisation to determine whether a company can list on the SME platform or the main board.

Currently, companies with post-issue paid-up share capital of up to ₹25 Cr can opt for the SME platform, subject to other eligibility conditions. 

In addition, companies in the ₹1,000 Cr to ₹4,000 Cr band choosing the SME platform would also have to submit restated consolidated financial statements under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) for the preceding three financial years, if they have not already adopted Ind AS.

If an IPO applicant’s estimated market capitalisation crosses the applicable threshold during the IPO process, it would have to refile under the relevant listing framework.

Minimum Profitability Requirements Raised

SEBI has proposed mandating SME IPO applicants to report an average operating profit of at least ₹3 Cr annually over the preceding three financial years, based on restated consolidated financial statements.

In contrast, the existing framework requires operating profit of at least ₹1 Cr in at least two of the preceding three fiscal years. However, the consultation paper refers to EBIT in its narrative, while existing provision mentioned EBITDA. This requires clarification.

Companies that fail the proposed profitability test could still list on the SME platform through an alternative route. They would have to use the book-building process and allocate at least 75% of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). If the required allocation is not achieved, the entire subscription amount would have to be refunded.

New Rules For Converted And Reorganised Businesses

SEBI has proposed changing the eligibility rules for SMEs seeking an IPO after converting from a proprietorship, partnership or limited liability partnership (LLP). These draft rules also cover companies undergoing qualifying business reorganisations.

Currently, such companies generally need to complete at least one full financial year before filing their draft IPO papers. Under the new proposal, they would need to complete four consecutive financial quarters from the date of conversion or qualifying reorganisation and submit at least one annual audited financial statement prepared after the change.

The proposal also covers acquisitions, succession and schemes of arrangement, where more than 50% of the revenue comes from businesses that previously operated as proprietorships, partnerships or LLPs. In such cases, the earlier business’ operating track record could be considered when assessing IPO eligibility.

The ₹10 Cr Cap On GCP Allocation May Go

SEBI has proposed removing the ₹10 Cr cap on the amount that the companies can allocate, from their IPO proceeds, towards general corporate purposes (GCP).

Currently, GCP allocation cannot exceed 15% of the amount raised or ₹10 Cr, whichever is lower. Under the proposal, the 15% limit would remain, but the fixed ₹10 Cr ceiling would be removed, allowing companies raising larger amounts to allocate more funds to general business needs.

SEBI Looks To Reshuffle OFS Rules

SEBI has also proposed a dedicated offer-for-sale (OFS) framework with a one-year holding requirement, subject to specified exemptions.

The draft framework also seeks to remove the existing 20% ceiling on the OFS component for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). The Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC) went a step further and suggested removing the 50% cap on a QIB’s pre-issue holding as well.

These exemptions, however, would not apply to companies using the alternative listing route after failing the proposed profitability test.

Lock-In Periods To Be Revised

SEBI has proposed revising the lock-in periods for promoters and other shareholders after an SME IPO. The draft changes include:

  • Minimum promoters’ contribution: The three-year lock-in on minimum promoter contribution would begin from the IPO allotment date. In contrast, the lock-in date is currently linked to the commencement of commercial production.
  • Promoter holdings above the minimum contribution: The existing staggered lock-in would be replaced with a uniform one-year lock-in.
  • Non-promoter pre-issue capital: The lock-in will reduce from the current one year to six months.
  • Promoter group holdings: A separate one-year lock-in would apply from the IPO allotment date.

Depositories could also mark shares that cannot be locked in electronically as non-transferable for the applicable period.

SEBI to Further Trim Minimum IPO Application Threshold

The markets regulator has proposed lowering the minimum application amount for SME IPOs to ₹1 Lakh from the existing requirement of more than ₹2 Lakh. Investors would have to apply for at least four lots worth a minimum of ₹25,000 each. The ₹2 Lakh minimum was introduced in March 2025 to limit participation by smaller retail investors.

The consultation paper also proposes aligning investor categories and allocation rules more closely with the mainboard framework, including the introduction of the ‘Retail Individual Investor’ category.

Under the regime, Issuers can also allocate up to 60% of the QIB portion to anchor investors in book-built issues. 

SEBI has also proposed increasing the minimum number of allottees from 200 to 500. Under the alternative route for companies failing the profitability test, up to 10% of the net offer would go to retail investors, up to 15% to NIIs and at least 75% to QIBs.

SME Shares Could Be Traded In Lots Of One

SEBI has proposed allowing investors to trade SME-listed shares in lots of one share, replacing the existing price-linked lot sizes.

The consultation paper notes that around 5% of unique PAN-based shareholders held odd-lot shares, on average. The proposed change could make it easier for investors to sell their entire holdings, but it will not change the minimum IPO application amount.

End For Mandatory Underwriting And Market-Making?

SEBI has proposed removing mandatory underwriting and market-making requirements for SME IPOs to reduce listing costs.

Currently, SME IPOs must be fully underwritten, with lead managers required to underwrite at least 15% of the issue themselves. Under the proposal, these requirements would be removed. The 75% QIB portion under the alternative listing route would not need to be underwritten.

Underwriting fees accounted for 49.52% and 38.41% of total SME IPO issue expenses on the NSE in FY25 and FY26, respectively. The corresponding figures for the BSE were 32.20% and 33.99%, according to SEBI.

The minimum subscription requirement would remain at 90% of the offer, excluding OFS. If the threshold is not met, application money would have to be refunded within four days of the issue closing.

SEBI has also proposed removing the requirement to maintain market-makers for three years after listing. Market-making fees accounted for 1.25%-4.20% of total issue expenses across the NSE and BSE in FY25 and FY26. The change could reduce costs but may affect liquidity in SME stocks with limited trading activity.

Changes To Mainboard Migration Rules

SEBI has proposed revising the rules that govern SME-listed companies, when they move to the mainboard.

Under the proposed framework, companies with a market capitalisation of ₹1,000 Cr or less would not have to migrate solely because of their valuation. Those valued above ₹1,000 Cr but below ₹4,000 Cr could voluntarily migrate, subject to the main board’s eligibility criteria. Companies valued at ₹4,000 Cr or more would have to mandatorily migrate.

Board approval would be sufficient for migration, without a shareholder vote. SEBI has also proposed removing the requirement to migrate when paid-up capital is likely to exceed ₹25 Cr and scrapping migration from the main board to the SME platform.

Companies already listed on the SME platform, when the new rules are notified, would continue to follow the existing migration framework.

item.title: Flipkart Group FY26: Revenue Nears ₹1.5 Lakh Cr, Loss Narrows To ₹8,468 Cr
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26…
item.content:encoded:
Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26), up from ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in the year ago fiscal. 

Meanwhile, its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25. 

The numbers reflect the performance of the Flipkart Group as a whole, rather than the standalone financials of the Flipkart ecommerce marketplace. The financial results come after the Walmart-backed ecommerce giant completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026. 

The restructuring brought the group’s holding structure back to India, ahead of a potential domestic public listing. The consolidated entity includes businesses such as Myntra and Cleartrip, alongside logistics, platform services and other specialised operations.

“As part of its re-domiciliation to India, (the) Flipkart Group is publishing consolidated financial results under Flipkart Internet Private Limited. The results reflect the group’s performance over the reporting period for the year ended March 2026 and provide a historical view of the business rather than a current trading update,” said the ecommerce giant in a blog post.

On the operational front, the company said that its gross margins rose 23% YoY in FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr during the fiscal. “Adjusted operating margin improved by 230 basis points, from -7.7% to -5.4%, supported by higher gross margins and lower overheads,” added the ecommerce major.

Flipkart also noted its adjusted operating business losses, before finance costs, tax, other income and exceptional items, narrowed by 17%, or around ₹1,600 Cr, during the fiscal under review.

However, this improvement in operating losses translated into only a marginal reduction in net losses. Flipkart attributed the higher net losses to higher finance costs, the derecognition of deferred tax assets recognised in earlier periods and certain exceptional items.

How Did Flipkart’s B2C Arm Perform?

Meanwhile, the ecommerce major’s B2C arm, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, reported a 19.3% YoY decline in revenue from operations to ₹16,295 Cr in FY26 compared with ₹20,202 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. 

Including other income of ₹744 Cr (down from ₹947 Cr in FY25), the B2C vertical’s total income stood at ₹17,039 Cr in FY26, 19.4% lower than ₹21,149 Cr in the previous fiscal. 

On the expenses front, Flipkart Internet Pvt Ltd’s total expenses fell 3.6% to ₹22,522 Cr from ₹23,361 Cr in FY25.

Overall, the B2C business’ net loss rose to ₹5,498 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,694 Cr a year earlier. Notably, the FY25 figures were restated to account for the business combination.

Where Did Flipkart Group Spend In FY26?

Despite the growing top line and narrowing losses, Flipkart Group’s total expenses rose 16% to ₹1.54 Lakh Cr in FY26 as against ₹1.33 Lakh Cr in the year-ago period. 

Purchase Of Traded Goods: This was the biggest cost-centre for the company. Expenses under this head climbed 17.4% YoY to ₹1.17 Lakh Cr in the fiscal under review.

Employee Benefit Expenses: The group’s employee benefit costs remained relatively flat at ₹8,376 Cr compared with ₹8,268 Cr in FY25.

Finance Costs: Expenditure under this bucket nearly doubled to ₹1,209 Cr from ₹649 Cr in FY25.

Logistics & Storage Service Charges: Expenses under this header stood at ₹15,154 Cr in FY26, up 28.9% from ₹11,759 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. The expense accounted for nearly 54% of the group’s total other expenses of ₹28,277 Cr in FY26, highlighting the cost of running its logistics, warehousing and delivery operations.

item.title: Origin Bags $20 Mn To Build Autonomous Construction Robots
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Emerging out of stealth mode, robotics startup Origin has raised $20 Mn (around ₹189 Cr) in a funding round co-led…
item.content:encoded:
Emerging out of stealth mode, robotics startup Origin has raised $20 Mn (around ₹189 Cr) in a funding round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. 

The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21. Angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla also participated in the fundraise. As part of the investment, Zacua Ventures’ founding partner Vivin Hegde has also joined the startup’s board as a director.

The startup said that the fresh capital will primarily be utilised to deploy its flagship OG-1 robot and build a fleet of construction robots. A chunk of the capital will also be used to support “large-scale” pilots with customers in the US and Europe and explore new use cases for bots.

“We think of Origin as a time machine for construction, helping crews complete work faster while moving the industry toward autonomous job sites. Wall finishing and painting are only our starting trades; our ambition is to automate the full range of interior trades so contractors can build faster with consistent quality,” said Origin cofounder and CEO Yogesh Ghaturle. 

Founded in 2025 by Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, the US-headquartered startup develops autonomous robotics for construction work. It aims to address widespread labour shortages in the construction sector and claims that its robots can work 3X faster than a human.

Its flagship robot, OG-1, is currently capable of automatically completing wall-finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding, and priming. The startup claims to have already deployed its robots at construction sites in  New York, adding that its bots are also being deployed across commercial spaces, apartments, data centers, hotels and warehouses. 

Under the hood, OG-1 is powered by a proprietary foundation model that the startup calls a construction action model. The model integrates a reasoning system to plan complex sub-tasks, an action policy to help it navigate autonomously and a controller for feedback-driven movement. 

Going forward, the startup plans to deploy 150 robots by the end of 2027. It is also exploring additional pilots for its offerings in countries like Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia. Origin also noted that incoming investor Zacua will support its expansion plans through its network of contractors, developers and manufacturers.

With the latest fundraise, Origin is eyeing a piece of the global construction robotics sector, which is projected to become a $12 Bn opportunity by 2036. Back home in India, startups like Pace Robotics and Flo Mobility are also raising big bucks to take a lead in the burgeoning space.

item.title: [Update] Zetwerk IPO Subscribed 23% On Day 1
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Update | October 10, 19:03 B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO received muted response on day one as it was subscribed…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 10, 19:03

B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO received muted response on day one as it was subscribed just 23%. The issue received bids for 4.17 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer.

The offer saw the highest subscription from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) who placed 2.96 Cr shares against their quota of 9.89 Cr shares, or 30% subscription. 

Retail individual investors bid for 74.32 Lakh shares out of the 3.42 Cr shares reserved for them, translating to a 22% subscription of their quota.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) placed bids for 44.08 Lakh shares, or just 9% of their quota of 5.13 Cr shares. 

Meanwhile, Zetwerk’s employees placed bids for 1.84 Lakh shares or subscribed to 26% of the 7 Lakh shares earmarked for them. 

Original | October 10, 14:24

B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO got off to a rather slow start today, receiving a mere 8% subscription as of 14:00 IST. Investors have placed bids for 1.50 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer, as per BSE data.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) have been the most bullish on the public float till now, placing the highest number of bids for 75.67 Lakh shares. However, this translated to a mere 8% subscription of their quota of 9.89 Cr shares.

Retail individual investors followed closely as they bid for 51.79 Lakh against 3.42 Cr shares reserved for them, translating to a 15% subscription of their quota.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed to just 4% of their earmarked portion, bidding for 21.55 Lakh out of 5.13 Cr shares allocated to them. 

Meanwhile, employees of the manufacturing company placed bids for 1.34 Lakh shares against the 7 Lakh shares reserved for them, subscribing to their quota by 19%.

Zetwerk’s IPO closes on October 19. The company set a price band of ₹143-₹151 per share for its IPO, indicating a valuation of around ₹25,583 Cr at the upper end. 

The issue comprises a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an offer for share component of up to 14.45 Cr shares, worth ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end, as per its RHP. 

Ahead of opening the issue, Zetwerk raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors yesterday. Domestic mutual funds including SBI Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund accounted for around 46% of the anchor book, while global institutional investors like Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and ADIA also picked up stake. 

Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Vishal Chaudhary,  Zetwerk operates a full-stack manufacturing platform serving businesses across industrial and consumer goods categories. 

It combines capacity from third-party suppliers and its own facilities to manage manufacturing orders across sectors including renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation.

The company has raised over $900 Mn in funding to date from investors like Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Accel India, Greenoaks Capital Partners, and D1 Capital Partners.

On the financial front, Zetwerk posted a consolidated net loss of ₹733 Cr in Q1 FY27 against operating revenue of ₹4,117.9 Cr.

item.title: Jio Financial Services Q2 Profit Halves YoY To ₹340 Cr
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Jio Financial Services’ consolidated net profit declined 51% to ₹340.4 Cr in the second quarter of the financial year ended…
item.content:encoded:
Jio Financial Services’ consolidated net profit declined 51% to ₹340.4 Cr in the second quarter of the financial year ended March 2027 (FY27) from ₹695 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

Operating revenue rose 73% to ₹1,699.3 Cr from ₹981.4 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also registered an other income of ₹13 Lakh during the quarter as against ₹21.1 Cr other income registered in the year-ago quarter.

Sequentially, net profit fell 59% from ₹830.3 Cr, while operating revenue declined 15.2% from ₹2,004.5 Cr.

The profit decline came amid higher expenses and the absence of dividend income during the quarter. Jio Financial Services had recorded dividend income of ₹269 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹508.6 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Total expenses for the quarter rose 167% YoY and 15% QoQ to ₹1,166.1 Cr. The uptick in costs was primarily driven by higher finance costs (up 325% YoY to ₹577.7 Cr) as the group expanded its borrowings to fund asset expansion, alongside elevated operational and staff costs as JFS continued to scale its digital financial ecosystem and super app ambitions.   

The company’s top line during the quarter was largely driven by sustained momentum and scale-up in core operational verticals — particularly disciplined loan book expansion at Jio Credit, robust growth in fee income from insurance broking, and expansion in asset management AUM under joint ventures. 

“FY27 marked yet another quarter of strong operational growth across our financial services platform. Our strategic playbook is now visibly taking shape with key global partnerships established across our core pillars — lending with Bank of America, investments with BlackRock, and insurance with Allianz Group. These marquee JVs bring world-class capabilities, institutional track records, and global best practices to India, while we drive growth on our digital platform and customer engagement ecosystem,” said JFS CEO and MD Hitesh Sethia.

Here’s a breakdown of the performance of the company’s key verticals during the quarter.

Jio Credit

Continuing its strong growth momentum, JFS’ NBFC arm saw its gross disbursements expand nearly double YoY to ₹13,135 Cr in Q2 FY27. Assets under management (AUM) jumped 154% YoY to ₹37,320 Cr. During the quarter, Bank of America entered into a landmark joint venture agreement with JFS to acquire up to 49.9% in Jio Credit for an investment of up to ₹18,268 Cr, subject to regulatory approvals.   

Jio Payments Bank

Jio Payments Bank continued to expand its footprint, with total income surging 213% YoY to ₹94 Cr in Q2 FY27. Customer deposits grew 53% YoY to ₹643 Cr, while CASA customer accounts expanded to around 40 Lakh accounts, with an average balance per customer of ₹1,573.

Jio Payment Solutions

The digital payments vertical recorded total payment value (TPV) of ₹14,682 Cr, representing an 8% YoY increase. Gross fee and commission income grew 70% YoY to ₹130 Cr, while net fee and commission income rose 74% YoY to ₹21 Cr.  Operating leverage and merchant mix optimisation helped expand the net processing margin to 14 bps.

Emerging Businesses

Jio BlackRock Asset Management saw its closing AUM expand 57% YoY to ₹22,746 Cr. Its Liquid Fund sustained quarterly average AUM above ₹10,000 Cr, ranking number one since inception, while the recently launched Prism Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) scaled to ₹478 Cr in AUM. 

Regulatory approval was also received from IFSCA for the JioBlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund (IFSC) in GIFT City. 

In insurance, Jio Insurance Broking facilitated insurance premiums worth ₹346 Cr in Q2 FY27, generating fee and commission income of ₹54 Cr (up 46% YoY).

On the digital front, the JioFinance App reached 3.2 Cr unique users and logged an average of about 36,000 product purchases per day. New ecosystem features introduced during the quarter included JioFinance+, JioFinance360 and JioSilver.

item.title: [Update] Tonbo Imaging IPO Subscribed 4X On Day 1, NIIs Lead Demand
item.dc:creator: Vinaykumar Rai
item.description: Update| October 15, 18:45 IST Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging’s ₹852 Cr IPO was oversubscribed 4X at the end of…
item.content:encoded:
Update| October 15, 18:45 IST

Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging’s ₹852 Cr IPO was oversubscribed 4X at the end of the first day of bidding, with investors bidding for 3.41 Cr shares against 85.26 Lakh shares on offer, according to BSE data.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) placed the highest bids, oversubscribing 5.96X of their quota. They placed bids for 1.08 Cr shares against 18.24 Lakh shares reserved for them. Within the NII category, the portion reserved for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 8.74X, while the portion for bids above ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 4.57X.

Retail investors bid for 1.36 Cr shares against their allocation of 42.56 Lakh shares, oversubscribing to 3.2X of the portion.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) picked up pace and bid for 95.43 Lakh shares against the 24.32 Lakh shares earmarked for them, translating to 3.92X of oversubscription.

The employee portion was subscribed 6.51X, with bids received for 91,203 shares against 14,000 shares on offer.

Original | October 15, 13:28 IST 

Defence tech startup Tonbo Imaging’s IPO was fully subscribed within hours of opening for bidding, with demand led by non-institutional investors (NIIs).

The public issue received bids for 1.26 Cr shares against 85.26 Lakh shares on offer, translating into an overall subscription of 1.47X as of 13:06 IST.

The NII portion was subscribed 2.73X, receiving bids for 49.82 Lakh shares against an allocation of 18.24 Lakh shares. Within this category, the portion for applications above ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 1.92X, while that for applications above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 4.36X.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) bid for just 7,707 shares against the 24.32 Lakh shares reserved for them. 

Meanwhile, retail investors bid for 75.07 Lakh shares against their allocation of 42.56 Lakh shares, subscribing to their portion 1.76X. The employee portion was booked 3.93X, attracting bids for 55,083 shares against 14,000 shares on offer.

The opening-day demand follows Tonbo’s ₹255.4 Cr anchor allocation ahead of the public issue. The startup allotted 36.5 Lakh shares to 43 anchor investors at ₹700 apiece.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for 57.7% of the anchor allocation, with 12 funds participating through 25 schemes. Other anchor investors included Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, WhiteOak Capital, Aranda Investments, and Allianz.

Tonbo has set a price band of ₹665–₹700 per share for its ₹852.1 Cr IPO, which will close on October 19. The issue comprises an OFS of up to 1.2 Cr shares, meaning the startup will receive no proceeds.

Selling shareholders include cofounders Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar, and Cecilia D’Souza, alongside CEAQ Technologies and Artiman Partners.

Inside Tonbo’s Defence Tech Business

Tonbo develops imaging and sensor systems for surveillance, reconnaissance, targeting, and other military applications. Its products include thermal weapon sights, driver-vision systems, fire-control systems, and missile seekers.

The startup outsources manufacturing to partners such as Kaynes Technology and Avalon Technology, while handling prototype development, system integration, and qualification testing in-house.

The IPO comes after a decline in Tonbo’s annual revenue and profit. Operating revenue fell 22.7% to ₹362.6 Cr in FY26 from ₹469.1 Cr in FY25, while net profit dropped 30.2% to ₹50.8 Cr from ₹72.8 Cr.

In Q1 FY27, Tonbo reported an operating revenue of ₹36 Cr and a net loss of ₹17.7 Cr.

item.title: Exclusive: Shopify To Bring Accelerated Checkout Service ‘Shop Pay’ To India
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Commerce technology company Shopify is preparing to bring its accelerated checkout product, Shop Pay, to India by the first quarter…
item.content:encoded:
Commerce technology company Shopify is preparing to bring its accelerated checkout product, Shop Pay, to India by the first quarter of 2027, sources told Inc42.

The company is in talks with payment orchestration platforms to integrate payment service providers, the sources added.

Shopify provides software that helps businesses build and run online stores, manage inventory and orders, and integrate payments and other services. A plethora of Indian D2C brands use its platform to run their online businesses.

These existing merchant relationships would give Shop Pay a route into India’s D2C checkout market, where startups such as GoKwik, Shopflo, Razorpay, and Shiprocket help brands improve purchase conversion and manage checkout. 

Shopify has not publicly confirmed the proposed launch timeline. Questions sent to the company remained unanswered till the time of publication.

What Shop Pay Adds To Shopify Checkout

Shop Pay allows customers to save their payment, shipping, and contact information to complete purchases faster across participating stores. Shopify claims the product can deliver up to 50% higher conversion than guest checkout.

Shopify already offers its native Shopify Checkout. Shop Pay adds an optional accelerated checkout experience using saved customer information. The product sits within Shopify’s broader commerce ecosystem, which includes storefront technology, merchant tools, and its consumer-facing Shop platform.

Whether Shop Pay replaces any of those services will depend on its India-specific features, payment support, and overall cost.

Competition Goes Beyond Faster Checkout

India’s checkout market includes Shiprocket’s Fastrr Checkout, Razorpay’s Magic Checkout, Cashfree Payments, GoKwik, and Shopflo, among others.

Shop Pay’s entry would bring these providers into closer competition with the platform on which some of their merchant customers already operate.

“GoKwik and Shopflo would need to find how to compete against a giant like Shopify. For others, checkout services contribute a small portion of revenue,” a person familiar with the payment gateway industry told Inc42 on condition of anonymity.

However, competing providers also have businesses and capabilities beyond accelerated checkout. GoKwik offers products spanning customer engagement, shopper identification, advertising, and returns management. Shopflo, meanwhile, is part of Pine Labs, which announced its acquisition in April 2026 to expand its payments and commerce offering.

Umair Mohammad, founder of Nitro Commerce, said Shopify’s brand recognition could give Shop Pay an advantage, but its entry would also widen merchants’ choices.

“Shopify will definitely have an advantage given that it is such a big brand. But more importantly, merchants will have more options to choose the best possible checkout solutions. Shop Pay’s entry does not automatically mean that other checkout services will struggle,” Mohammad said.

He added that checkout providers offer capabilities beyond saving addresses, including return-to-origin (RTO) intelligence and payment orchestration.

“So there are multiple factors at play, and a lot will also depend on pricing and how they position Shop Pay,” he said.

Pricing And Integration In Focus

Shop Pay’s India pricing has not been confirmed. A comparison with existing providers would need to account for any checkout charges, payment-processing fees, and applicable Shopify transaction fees.

While Native integration could make Shop Pay attractive to existing Shopify merchants, the incentive to switch would depend on whether it can meet their payment and operational requirements at a competitive cost.

For competing providers, the challenge would be to demonstrate the value of their broader services alongside faster checkout.

item.title: Udaan’s FY26 Revenue Rises 13% To ₹5,134 Cr, Loss Narrows To ₹852 Cr
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: B2B ecommerce unicorn Udaan’s operating revenue grew 12.6% to ₹5,134 Cr in the financial year ended March 2026 (FY26) from…
item.content:encoded:
B2B ecommerce unicorn Udaan’s operating revenue grew 12.6% to ₹5,134 Cr in the financial year ended March 2026 (FY26) from ₹4,561 Cr in FY25.

The startup’s net loss narrowed 19.4% to ₹851.5 Cr from ₹1,055.4 Cr in the previous fiscal, according to its financial statements.

The recovery follows an uneven revenue trajectory — a 40% decline in FY23, marginal growth of 1.7% in FY24, and a 20% fall in FY25. During this period, Udaan also closed a $114 Mn Series G funding round in June 2025 at a 59% valuation dip.

In a LinkedIn post, Udaan’s senior vice president Vishnu Menon attributed the improvement to the startup’s focus on profitable growth, operational efficiency, and tighter execution across its markets.

Over the 10 quarters from Q4 CY23 to Q1 CY26, the company’s revenue grew at a CAGR of around 25%, while its contribution margin improved by nearly 500 basis points and EBITDA burn declined by around 70%, Menon said.

Menon attributed this progress to its cluster-led operating model, which focuses on accountability for performance at the city and category levels, deeper operations in existing markets, and tighter cost controls.

However, Udaan’s financial statements flagged material uncertainty that could cast significant doubt on the group’s ability to continue as a going concern.

At the end of FY26, the group’s current liabilities exceeded its current assets by ₹1,391 Cr, while its total liabilities exceeded its total assets by ₹790.9 Cr.

The startup said it received additional funding after the financial year ended and expects revenue growth and cost-cutting measures to improve operating cash flows.

Founded in 2016 by former Flipkart executives Amod Malviya, Sujeet Kumar, and Vaibhav Gupta, Udaan operates a B2B digital marketplace connecting manufacturers, brands, wholesalers, and retailers, including kirana stores, chemists, and general merchants, through a mobile app.

Udaan’s Bumpy FY27

Despite the improvement in its FY26 financial performance, Udaan faced fresh challenges in the ongoing fiscal, with creditors initiating insolvency proceedings against its offshore parent over a bond default.

Creditors, including Tor Investment Management, Samena Capital, and Arena Investors, initiated proceedings in the Singapore High Court after Udaan’s offshore holding entity, Trustroot Internet Pvt Ltd, defaulted on $170 Mn worth of compulsorily convertible notes due on June 30.

Confirming the development at the time, Udaan told Inc42 that the proceedings concerned its offshore holding company and would not have any material impact on its operations in India.

Later in July, Udaan announced a proposed $160 Mn financing transaction, comprising fresh equity, new debt, and conversion of existing debt into equity.

Last month, Udaan announced an agreement to acquire Swiggy’s retail distribution business, LYNK, in an all-share transaction valuing the business at ₹500 Cr. Swiggy also announced plans to invest another ₹75 Cr in Udaan’s parent entity.

Udaan expects the acquisition to expand its retail distribution capabilities and market reach, while improving efficiency across the combined network.

Udaan Bets On Private Labels, Institutional Sales

Udaan is also looking to improve its revenue mix and margins through private labels and its institutional procurement business, horeca360.

According to Menon, private labels now account for 15-25% of staples sales across Udaan’s operating cities. He expects the segment to improve margins and capture a larger share of customers’ spending using its existing sourcing and distribution infrastructure.

Meanwhile, horeca360, which caters to hotels, restaurants, caterers, and institutional buyers, expanded into Hyderabad and Chennai during FY26. The business aims to deepen customer relationships and improve utilisation of Udaan’s supply chain network.

Menon said it would continue to focus on improving revenue quality, strengthening execution at the city level, and increasing operating efficiency as it works towards sustained profitability and a public listing.

item.title: Fairfax Proposes To Transfer Go Digit Stake To IDBI Bank
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings has proposed transferring all its interests in insurtech company Go Digit General Insurance and its…
item.content:encoded:
Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings has proposed transferring all its interests in insurtech company Go Digit General Insurance and its affiliate Go Digit Life Insurance to IDBI Bank.

Separately, Fairfax India Holdings has also proposed transferring its entire stake in IIFL Capital Services to the lender.

The proposals follow the Indian government’s selection of a wholly owned Fairfax Financial subsidiary as the “strategic buyer” for a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank. Under its bid, Fairfax would acquire the controlling stake for approximately ₹52,878 Cr ($5.6 Bn), at ₹81 per share.

Fairfax said the proposed transfers would take place at the respective market prices of the holdings, subject to applicable laws and regulatory approvals. Both transfers would require approvals from RBI, SEBI, and other relevant authorities. The Go Digit transaction would also require clearance from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI).

“We are very excited about the prospect of combining Digit with IDBI Bank as it would significantly strengthen Digit’s distribution footprint, allowing us to continue our growth and service offerings for the benefit of all Indians,” Go Digit CEO Kamesh Goyal said.

Fairfax chairman and CEO Prem Watsa said the proposed arrangement would allow IDBI Bank to distribute insurance products through Digit Insurance, while offering investment banking and wealth management services through IIFL Capital.

Fairfax’s Go Digit Investment History

Fairfax has been a key investor in Go Digit since the insurtech’s early years. It holds its interest through wholly owned subsidiary FAL Corporation and has invested alongside Goyal and his entity, Oben Ventures LLP.

Their holdings were routed through Go Digit Infoworks Services Pvt Ltd (GDISPL), the insurer’s holding company. In its IPO papers, Go Digit disclosed that FAL Corporation held 45.25% of GDISPL’s equity capital, while Goyal and Oben Ventures held 14.96% and 39.79%, respectively.

Go Digit listed in May 2024, raising ₹1,125 Cr through a fresh issue of shares. GDISPL held a controlling 72.98% stake in the insurer as of June 30, 2026.

Fairfax’s ownership is indirect, with FAL Corporation, Fairfax Asia Ltd, Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd, FFHL Group, Falcon Insurance Public Company Ltd, and Fairfax (Barbados) International Corp forming part of Go Digit’s promoter group.

In December 2025, Go Digit’s board approved a scheme to amalgamate GDISPL into the listed insurer. Under the proposal, GDISPL would be dissolved without being wound up, making Fairfax, Goyal, and Oben Ventures direct shareholders in Go Digit.

In a June rating note, CRISIL estimated that Fairfax’s holding would rise to 57.28% on a fully diluted basis following the amalgamation, factoring in its equity and compulsorily convertible preference shares in GDISPL. Goyal and Oben Ventures’ combined holding would fall to 14.92%.

The Competition Commission of India approved the proposed amalgamation on July 28. This is a separate transaction from Fairfax’s proposed transfer of its Digit interests to IDBI Bank.

Meanwhile, Go Digit reported a 37.5% decline in net profit to ₹86.4 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹138.3 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its gross premium written fell 8.4% to ₹2,730.9 Cr from ₹2,981.8 Cr.

Shares of Go Digit were trading 0.14% lower at ₹283.50 on the BSE.

item.title: Centre Directs Telcos To Display Caller Names From November 1
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Ministry Of Communications’ Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has directed telecom operators to roll out calling name presentations (CNAP) across…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry Of Communications’ Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has directed telecom operators to roll out calling name presentations (CNAP) across their service areas from November 1, 2026. This will allow users to see the caller’s name alongside their phone number without necessarily saving contact details beforehand.

The rollout follows an amendment to the definition of calling line identification (CLI) under the unified licence agreement, which will also take effect on November 1. 

The revised definition includes the caller’s name as recorded in telecom operators’ subscriber databases. However, contacts saved will continue to remain unchanged. 

CNAP will be enabled by default on 4G and higher-generation wireless networks, without requiring users to opt in. Its rollout on 2G and 3G networks and landline connections will be examined separately.

Callers who have activated the calling line identification restriction (CLIR) facility to hide their identity will be exempt from this.

The originating telecom service provider (TSP) must maintain a database linking subscribers’ names to their telephone identifiers, which the recipient’s operator will query to display the caller’s name without retaining it after the call ends.

DoT has also allowed business and bulk-connection users to display a preferred name instead of the one in their subscriber records, provided it is backed by a trademark registered with the Trade marks registry or a trade name registered on the goods and services tax (GST) portal. These users can also request changes, subject to verification

Telecom operators, including the likes of Jio, Airtel, Vodafone, must verify the supporting documents before approving the change.

The guidelines require telecom operators to protect users’ privacy by ensuring caller names are not stored after a call ends. They must also ensure their networks can handle caller identification requests without affecting service quality and set up systems to address complaints related to the service.

The rollout follows trials conducted by telecom operators on 4G and higher-generation networks and the TRAI’s recommendations issued in February 2024. 

Last year in October, TRAI supported making CNAP available by default, departing from its earlier proposal to activate the service only upon user request.

item.title: AI Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In October
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: India’s AI story is moving beyond the model. Until last year, the big question in Indian boardrooms was which large…
item.content:encoded:
India’s AI story is moving beyond the model. Until last year, the big question in Indian boardrooms was which large language model (LLM) enterprises should standardise on. Now, as AI agents move from answering questions to executing tasks, the focus is shifting to what these agents can do for businesses, which workflows they should handle, and how enterprises can measure their performance.

In September, Inc42 reported that Swiggy is opening food delivery, Instamart, Dineout, and Scenes to external AI agents. Through four Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and 66 tools, the company lets AI assistants outside its app build carts, place orders, and book tables. The same month, we explored how Flipkart is reworking product discovery for a future where customers may no longer begin their shopping journeys with keyword searches. 

As AI agents take on more tasks, enterprises must look beyond the underlying models to the systems that make them useful and reliable. That means building workflows that allow agents to execute tasks effectively and evaluation systems that measure whether they deliver the intended results. 

Meanwhile, investor interest in the sector remains strong. Indian AI startups raised $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY, according to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026. 

Against this backdrop, Inc42 returns with the 13th edition of the AI Startups To Watch series. This edition features five emerging ventures tackling distinct opportunities: agentic commerce, screen-free learning, AI agent reliability, automated customer conversations and AI-powered recruitment.

Here are the five startups from the 13th edition of Inc42’s AI Startups To Watch.

Editor’s Note: This is not a ranking. The startups featured here are a curated selection by the Inc42 editorial team and are listed alphabetically.

 Agnost AI | Keeping A Closer Eye On AI Agents 

A chatbot that gives a wrong answer frustrates users. An AI agent that fails silently can cost a business its customers. Users may correct it, repeat their requests or abandon the interaction altogether, while dashboards continue to record the exchange as a success.

Agnost AI is building tools to detect these failures and help teams fix them. Founded in 2025 by Shubham Palriwala and Parth Ajmera, the platform monitors AI agents in production by analysing their conversations with users. It identifies recurring problems, flags instances where users correct the agent or abandon a task, and traces failures back through the agent’s tool calls to identify what went wrong. 

It then suggests fixes and tests them against the conversations in which the agent failed before deployment. It adds cases where fixes work to a regression test suite to help prevent the same errors from recurring.

Agnost integrates with agent-building frameworks such as LangChain and CrewAI, and counts Exa and Comp AI among its users. It is backed by Y Combinator, Entrepreneurs First and Transpose Platform Management. The startup is targeting the agentic AI monitoring and observability tools market, estimated at $500 Mn in 2025 and projected to reach $2 Bn by 2030, growing at a 30.1% CAGR.

Dialflo | AI Voice Agents With ROI

Many Indian enterprises have spent the past two years experimenting with AI voice bots, only to find it difficult to measure their impact. The challenge isn’t just getting an AI agent to handle calls, but understanding how well it performs, what business outcomes it delivers, and when human intervention is needed.

Bengaluru-based Dialflo is building a platform to address this gap. Founded in 2024 by Abhishek Kumar, the startup combines AI voice agents and human agents in a single contact centre, helping businesses automate customer interactions while tracking their outcomes.

Its voice agents handle high-volume tasks such as qualifying leads, verifying cash-on-delivery orders to reduce returns, recovering abandoned carts and providing multilingual customer support around the clock. What sets Dialflo apart is its focus on attribution: it scores each conversation and links it to a business outcome, helping customer experience teams measure the revenue generated by calls alongside the costs saved.

This focus comes as the global call centre AI market expands, with its value projected to rise from $1.9 Bn in 2024 to $7.1 Bn by 2030, at a CAGR of 23.8%, according to Grand View Research.

Dialflo works with more than 10 enterprise customers, including Tata Digital, Intugine and Careernet. 

HireBound | AI Agents For End-To-End Hiring

Recruiters often spend a lot of time chasing candidates, screening resumes and conducting repetitive initial interviews rather than evaluating the people best suited for a role. As hiring volumes grow, these tasks become harder to manage without adding to recruitment teams.

Bengaluru-based HireBound is using AI agents to automate much of this work. Founded in 2024 by Sharad Vij and Kumar Vikramaditya, the startup aims to help recruiters move candidates through the hiring process faster.

Its platform uses separate agents for sourcing, screening and evaluation. These agents engage candidates through voice calls, WhatsApp, text messages and email, gathering information to assess their suitability for a role. Looking to capitalise on the growth of India’s HR tech market, projected to reach $2.3 Bn by 2034, the platform integrates with companies’ existing applicant tracking systems and human resource management systems. Its customers include staffing firms and enterprise talent acquisition teams in India and the US.

HireBound has conducted more than 3 Mn candidate conversations and trained its systems on over 2 Mn resumes and 30,000 job openings. It raised $2 Mn (₹18.2 Cr) in a seed round led by Kalaari Capital, with participation from Antler, Infinyte Club and CareerNet. The startup is targeting a fivefold increase in annual recurring revenue over the next year.

MyWonder | Screen-Free AI Learning Companion

For children aged three to ten, finding ways to make learning engaging without relying on screens remains a challenge. 

MyWonder is building a screen-free alternative. Founded in 2024 by Chandramouli K, formerly of Amazon and RedBus, and Venkat Potluri, formerly of Flipkart and ZestMoney, the startup wants to make learning interactive through voice-led play.

Its WonderPod combines a voice-first device with figurines and cards that unlock stories, quizzes and games. A conversational AI layer adapts to each child’s speech and learning level, while a companion app lets parents track activities and manage content access. The startup also sources content through publisher partnerships.

MyWonder operates in India’s tech toys market, expected to reach about $3.6 Bn by 2030, expanding at a CAGR of 14.7%.

Tru Commerce | Commerce Infra For AI Agents

Shopping is moving into chat windows, where consumers can ask AI assistants to recommend products and receive a shortlist. But even when brands appear in these recommendations, shoppers cannot always buy from them directly. Many brands lack product catalogues that AI agents can read and checkout systems that work within these conversations.

Tru Commerce is building the infrastructure to bridge that gap. Founded in 2024 as Asva AI by Viren Inaniyan and Umang Chhaparia, the startup rebranded this year to focus on helping brands sell through AI agents.

Its platform has three core functions. It converts product pages into structured data that AI agents can understand, connects brands’ existing stores to agent-led checkouts through protocols such as MCP, ACP and UCP, and tracks brand mentions, product recommendations and orders attributed to AI agents. Brands remain the merchant of record and retain their customer relationships.

Tru Commerce works with Amazon, ITC MasterChef, MyMuse, Provogue and House of Zelena. The startup is targeting the global agentic commerce market, estimated at $1.9 Bn in 2025 and projected to reach $54.2 Bn by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 39.81%.

With inputs from Venu Rathore & Akshit Pushkarna

item.title: How Ubiqedge Is Giving Old Industrial Machines An AIoT Upgrade
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Nobody on a factory floor wakes up wanting AI, Internet of Things (IoT) systems or a smarter dashboard. Their job…
item.content:encoded:
Nobody on a factory floor wakes up wanting AI, Internet of Things (IoT) systems or a smarter dashboard. Their job is simply to keep machines running, production moving, and compliance headaches at bay. For factories, this also means keeping track of groundwater extraction, air quality and other metrics, which regulators now expect enterprises to monitor and report.

For decades, this grunt work rested on manual readings. A flow meter installed on a borewell would tell a factory how much water was being pumped out. Someone would note the reading, compile it and submit it to the relevant authority. The system worked, but it was slow, fragmented and vulnerable to inaccurate reporting. 

Now, as regulatory expectations shift towards IoT-based monitoring of industrial assets, this challenge of compliance has become more urgent. Enterprises may not necessarily care about deploying another layer of technology, but they care about avoiding the fines and disruption that follow non-compliance. 

Another major issue facing enterprise compliance is that most manufacturers, which supply industrial monitoring equipment, are not built to offer software, AI and connected-device capabilities. 

“Industries had long relied on flow meters for manual readings. When IoT monitoring became mandatory, they turned to their existing flow meter vendors for compliance support. However, most OEMs lacked expertise in IoT, AI, and software,” says Ubiqedge cofounder Visat Patel.

This is where Mumbai-based Ubiqedge appears to have found its niche. Founded in 2024 by Patel, Archit Khandelwal, Akhilesh Thorat and Hetvi Shah, the startup is building a full-stack artificial internet of things (AIoT) platform for monitoring and managing industrial infrastructure.

Its hardware platform, KLEON, and AI-powered software layer, SAMASTH, are designed to help industrial equipment makers and system integrators convert conventional machines into automated systems. Earlier this year, the Mumbai-based startup raised ₹10 Cr in a seed round led by Piper Serica. 

A Second Shot At Industrial IoT

For Patel, Ubiqedge is his second attempt at building an industrial IoT company. An alumnus of IIT Bombay, Patel began his entrepreneurial journey in his final year of college. He holds two patents – one in biomedical devices and another in agritech. 

Before Ubiqedge, he founded Ushwa, an IoT startup that operated for nearly eight years before it was shut down. 

By his own admission, Patel said that the technology was sound, but the go-to-market (GTM) approach was wrong, and the business couldn’t scale past a certain point. This experience left the founders with a clearer understanding of why industrial IoT deployments often fail to move beyond pilots.

“We identified that while AI and IoT tools are good individually, industries aren’t very comfortable engaging with this technology. A lot of large companies have deployed this tech at a cost of ₹50 Lakh or a couple of crores, gotten a good overview, but then nothing concrete has come out of the solution. This has weakened industry confidence in the technology’s scalability,” Patel said.

Determined not to repeat the past mistakes, Patel regrouped his founding team, including Khandelwal, Thorat and Shah, to rethink industrial IoT deployment from the ground up. The four cofounders quickly zeroed in on three persistent bottlenecks. 

  • Technology creators lacked the bandwidth to support varied industrial use cases
  • OEMs also lacked the expertise to develop IoT and AI layers around their machines
  • Technicians on the ground were often intimidated by complex connected systems.

Ubiqedge was built around solving this three-way problem. Rather than asking factories to adopt a new tech stack from scratch, the startup was envisaged with the idea of making industrial AI and IoT simple enough to deploy at scale.

Turning Machines Into Connected Assets

To overcome traditional enterprise sales resistance, the startup deploys a novel distribution strategy. Ubiqedge doesn’t sell directly to factories. It sells to OEMs and system integrators, who then bundle Ubiqedge’s hardware and software with their own equipment.

Powering this bundled model is a plug-and-play tech architecture designed to upgrade legacy machinery without disrupting existing operations.

At the heart of Ubiqedge’s tech stack is KLEON, a hardware device that is integrated with industrial equipment. It reads the data generated by the equipment, stores it and sends it to the cloud. The device can communicate with nearly any sensor protocol and can operate through SIM connectivity, Wi-Fi or LAN.

Take a factory borewell as an example. The flow meter attached to the borewell measures the volume of groundwater being extracted. Ubiqedge’s device connects to this meter, captures the reading and transmits the data to the cloud.

The software layer, SAMASTH, then converts that raw information into a usable operating and compliance system. It can show the factory owner live groundwater consumption, retain a year of historical data, automatically forward required data to government servers and send alerts when usage approaches a limit set by the owner.

The system can go a step further. Using the same hardware-software combination, a factory can automatically shut off the borewell pump once the licensed extraction limit is reached. In this sense, the startup is not merely digitising a flow meter, but turning it into an automated compliance tool.

“A common failure mode with tech adoption is offering technology that just notifies you of a problem without doing anything about it. We always deliver a baseline ROI (return on investment) automatically, without requiring further action,” Patel said.

The startup currently caters to four use cases: smart water management, solar photovoltaic remote monitoring and control, smart concrete management and air-quality monitoring.

Separately, Ubiqedge is also working on an AI-driven configuration layer to make its platform more adaptable for OEMs and system integrators. The idea is to let a client describe a new use case in a prompt: which sensors need to be connected, which data points need tracking and what kind of dashboard needs to be created. 

The system would then generate the relevant firmware (the software layer that runs on the hardware) as well as the analytics dashboard, without requiring programming. This could make it easier for factories to deploy solutions across specialised industrial needs without waiting for custom engineering work for each new application.

Smart Hardware, Steady Margins

On the business front, Ubiqedge operates on a dual-revenue model. Besides one-time hardware sales, the startup also earns revenue from its software via an annual subscription model. 

Piggybacking on the distribution networks and customer relationships, the Mumbai-based venture claims to have already onboarded more than 100 direct customers, over 8,000 end users and roughly 30,000 devices deployed through its OEM and system-integrator network.

On the back of this, the startup claims to have closed FY26 with a revenue of around ₹7 Cr, with double-digit profit margins. It also claims to have been cash-positive since its first year of operations.

Going ahead, Ubiqedge plans to expand its footprint globally, with an eye on the Middle East first. 

But the road ahead may not be easy as the AIoT startup eyes its next stage of growth.

While its servers are currently hosted in India to comply with domestic data localisation norms, moving overseas will require the startup to set up dedicated regional data infrastructure in each of these geographies.

Hardware adds another set of constraints. While manufacturing is outsourced to Indian contract manufacturers, Ubiqedge still relies on Chinese connectivity chipsets. Any supply disruption, price volatility or component shortage could affect delivery timelines and margins.

The startup’s dependence on OEMs and system integrators, rather than factories, also limits its control over sales cycles, installation quality and the end customer relationship. Ubiqedge must ensure that its partners can explain, deploy and support its products without turning the implementation into a complex project.

But Ubiqedge’s biggest challenge will likely be overcoming the scepticism that industrial clients have developed after years of expensive but underwhelming IoT deployments. 

For now, with a cash-positive business and a fresh seed round, Ubiqedge is looking to deepen its presence in India while preparing for overseas expansion. The bigger test will be whether its partner-led model can scale across industries and geographies without losing the simplicity that forms the core of its pitch.

item.title: Confido Health Raises $12.5 Mn To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: US-based AI healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 Mn (about ₹119 Cr) in a Series A extension led by…
item.content:encoded:
US-based AI healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 Mn (about ₹119 Cr) in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn.

Existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures also participated in the round. Healthcare private equity investor Justin Saks has joined the startup as an investor and board adviser.

The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its CareOS platform across healthcare organisations with multiple sites and develop AI agents for additional workflows and medical specialities.

Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops AI agents to automate administrative tasks for healthcare providers, including patient calls, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills, and payment collection.

Its CareOS platform integrates with more than 50 healthcare systems, including electronic health records, practice management software, and billing platforms. This allows providers to automate tasks across their existing systems without replacing their technology infrastructure.

Confido Health initially focused on voice AI for patient calls before expanding into broader healthcare administration. Its platform connects related tasks, allowing a patient interaction to trigger follow-up work such as scheduling an appointment, processing a prescription refill, or collecting a payment.

The startup primarily targets healthcare groups operating across multiple sites, particularly those backed by private equity firms. Its distribution strategy involves working with private equity investors to secure introductions to their portfolio companies.

Confido Health said it serves 3,200 providers across more than 1,500 sites in 27 US states, with its AI agents enabling one in 50 Americans to access healthcare. It claimed 15-fold growth since its previous funding round but did not specify the metric.

The startup reported AI handling rates above 95% across key end-to-end administrative workflows. It said deployments added operational capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months, while patient satisfaction averaged 4.55 out of five across approximately one million tasks.

The fundraise comes amid investor bets on AI applications across healthcare, from administrative automation to patient guidance and early disease detection.

Earlier, Inc42 reported that AI health companion startup August AI was in talks to raise about $4 Mn from Peak XV Partners. The startup helps users understand symptoms, prescriptions, medications, and medical reports.

Earlier this year, Practo cofounder Shashank ND’s new venture Cent raised about $5 Mn from his family office OneFlow Holdings and South Park Commons. Cent uses AI and health data to detect critical diseases early.

Indian healthtech startups raised $93 Mn across 13 deals in Q3 2026 till September 24.

item.title: Shamrock AI Bags $5 Mn To Help Enterprises Deploy AI Agents Reliably
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI has raised $5 Mn (about ₹47.4 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Endiya…
item.content:encoded:
Enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI has raised $5 Mn (about ₹47.4 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.

The Shillong-headquartered startup said it will use its first institutional funding round to accelerate product development, expand its team across India and the US, scale go-to-market efforts, and expand its presence in the Middle East.

Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Anuraag Nallapati, and Michael Gallagher, Shamrock AI is building an agentic assurance platform that helps large enterprises deploy AI agents across critical business processes, ensuring they operate reliably in complex environments.

Its platform uses an Enterprise Business Knowledge Graph to connect business processes, systems, data, and configurations, giving AI agents context about how an enterprise operates.

The startup is initially focusing on using AI agents to automate testing across large enterprise resource planning (ERP) transformations, including SAP S/4HANA migrations.

Shamrock AI said continuously testing and validating business processes helps its platform build an increasingly accurate representation of an enterprise’s operations. It plans to use this foundation to extend into data observability and autonomous business process automation.

The startup said it already serves multiple Fortune 500 customers, including a Fortune 100 AI hardware manufacturer and a Fortune 100 healthcare company.

Shamrock AI expects 70%-80% of its workforce to be based in India and plans to build a client-facing team in the US. Besides its Shillong headquarters, it has offices in Hyderabad and San Francisco.

item.content:encoded:
Jio All Set For Its Mega IPO 

Reliance’s digital crown is heading down the Dalal Street. In what could be India’s biggest IPO yet, Jio Platforms has filed its RHP with SEBI for a ₹30,213 Cr listing. So, what does Jio Platforms’ IPO stack look like?

India’s Biggest IPO: Jio Platforms’ public issue, which consists entirely of a fresh issue of 27 Cr equity shares, will open for subscription on October 21 and close on October 23. The digital giant has set a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 per share for its issue, which will value the company at a nifty ₹10.3 Lakh Cr. 

Who Owns Jio? Reliance Industries holds 66.43% of the company, while big tech giants Meta and Google own 9.98% and 7.73%, respectively. Beyond the captable, Jio Platforms will use ₹27,500 Cr of the IPO proceeds to repay borrowings. The remaining ₹2,713 Cr will support corporate purposes, growth, capex, working capital and marketing.

The Number Game: Jio Platforms is stepping into D-Street with a profitable stack and robust top line growth.

Here is a quick look at Jio Platforms’ Q1 FY27 numbers:

  • Operating revenue rose 11.8% YoY to ₹39,173 Cr
  • Net profit jumped 9.2% YoY to ₹7,764 Cr
  • EBITDA improved 15.1% YoY to ₹20,865 Cr

Jio Mighty Scale: What works for the digital giant’s IPO is its massive subscriber base, nationwide 5G network and strong financial growth. On top of this, Jio’s expansion into AI, data centres and SaaS could unlock new revenue streams for the company, while the debt repayment will lower interest costs and strengthen the balance sheet. The issue’s record size and RIL’s backing could further support demand.

The Valuation Friction: Despite the tailwinds, Jio’s sky-high valuation could face pushback from public investors. With wireless subscriber growth plateauing, future earnings rely heavily on ARPU hikes that could lead to user churn. Additionally, high capex for satcom rollout and infrastructure upgrades could further squeeze margins and cash flows.

With the ball now in investors’ court, here is all about Jio Platforms gearing up for India’s biggest IPO till date…

From The Editor’s Desk

Zetwerk’s Anchor Haul

  • Ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its IPO today, the B2B manufacturing startup raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors. Zetwerk allotted 14.91 Cr shares to anchor investors at ₹151 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band.
  • Zetwerk’s ₹5,012 Cr public issue comprises a fresh issue worth ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS component of up to 14.45 Cr shares. At the upper end of its ₹143-₹151 IPO price band, the public offering values the company at around ₹25,583 Cr.
  • Separately, defence tech startup Tonbo Imaging has also raised ₹255 Cr from 43 anchor investors ahead of the opening of its IPO. It has set a price band of ₹665-₹700 per share for its ₹852 Cr IPO, which consists entirely of an OFS of up to 1.22 Cr shares.

Groww’s Q2 Profit Run

  • The investment tech company’s consolidated net profit zoomed 54% YoY to ₹724.7 Cr in Q2 FY27. This came on the back of operating revenue rising 47% YoY to ₹1,501.5 Cr as well as healthy growth in margin trading and commodity derivatives verticals.
  • Consolidated EBITDA improved 60% YoY to ₹969 Cr in the quarter ended September 2026. However, expenses continued to bite and rose 28.5% YoY to ₹555.9 Cr in the quarter under review.
  • Going forward, the company expects businesses with lower penetration, such as MTF and commodity derivatives, to grow faster and contribute a larger share of its income in the coming quarters.

Scimplify Nets $25 Mn

  • The speciality chemical manufacturing startup has raised ₹238 Cr in a strategic funding round led by Hitachi Ventures to expand its R&D and manufacturing capabilities, enter new emerging categories and scale its agentic AI offering. 
  • Founded in 2023, Scimplify offers end-to-end sourcing and manufacturing of speciality chemicals. It operates a network of more than 500 manufacturing partners and caters to more than 1,000 clients across 40 countries. It has raised $80 Mn to date.
  • Scimplify operates in the broader Indian deeptech sector, which continues to draw investor attention on the back of regulatory push, subsidies, a thriving talent pool and growing demand. The sector raised $290 Mn in Q3 2026, up 176% YoY.

Infotech Acquires Zluri

  • The IT advisory firm has acquired the Bengaluru-based SaaS startup for an undisclosed amount. Once the deal materialises, Zluri will operate as a standalone division within Infotech and will retain its product development and core engineering teams.
  • Founded in 2020, Zluri helps businesses track and manage all the digital tools their employees use. The startup claims to cater to over 250 enterprise clients globally and has raised more than $32 Mn in funding to date. 
  • The deal is in line with an emerging trend of global companies acquiring Indian SaaS startups to expand their capabilities. Homegrown SaaS major Freshworks acquired Torii earlier this week, while Adobe acquired Peak XV-backed Rilo last month.

Traya Eyes ₹300 Cr

  • The haircare startup is in talks with Belgian VC giant Verlinvest to raise around $31 Mn. With the talks still in early stages, the proposed round could value the startup at up to ₹3,000 Cr and will include both primary and secondary components.
  • The funding talks come amid a sharp uptick in Traya’s top line. The startup is said to be currently clocking an annualised revenue rate of ₹900 Cr to ₹1,000 Cr. It has also been expanding its offline presence and operates more than 20 centres across India.
  • Founded in 2019, Traya combines hair assessment, recommendation algorithm and doctor approval to offer personalised hair treatment plans for customers. It reported a net loss of ₹22.5 Cr in FY25 against a revenue of ₹338.4 Cr.

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How EV91 Is Electrifying India’s Last-Mile Deliveries

India’s delivery economy is growing fast. But gig workers still face fragmented access to EVs, financing, charging, maintenance and fleet support. To solve this, EV91 is building an integrated electric mobility platform that connects riders, EVs and delivery businesses under one roof.

An Electric Ecosystem: Founded in 2023, EV91 initially used to supply electric two-wheelers to delivery workers. It has since expanded into EV subscriptions, fleet management, charging, battery swapping and rider support. With this, it is positioning itself as a full-stack platform for last-mile delivery.

Electrifying Last Mile: The startup’s rider app allows delivery partners to rent EVs, find delivery jobs and access charging and battery-swapping services. For aggregator platforms, the startup offers fleet management solutions and a steady supply of gig workers. EV91 currently operates in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi-NCR and Mumbai. 

Growing Steadily: The startup claims to have completed 10 Lakh orders in FY25, with more than 600 EVs and 1,000+ riders. EV91 is targeting the homegrown last-mile delivery market, which is projected to become a $5.5 Bn economy by 2030. 

As delivery platforms seek cleaner and more reliable logistics, can EV91 build the backbone for India’s last-mile deliveries?

Ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its public issue on October 15, defence tech startup Tonbo Imaging has raised ₹255.4 Cr from anchor investors.

According to BSE data, the startup allotted 36.5 Lakh equity shares to 43 anchor investors at ₹700 apiece, the upper band of its IPO price band. 

Of the total anchor allocation, 21.1 Lakh shares, or 57.7%, were lapped up by 12 domestic mutual funds via a total of 25 schemes. The domestic mutual funds that anchored the round included SBI Infrastructure Fund, Axis Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Services Fund, Mirae Asset, Canara Robeco Mutual Fund, among others. 

Other investors who participated in the round included Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, WhiteOak Capital, Aranda Investments, Allianz, among others.

With this, Tonbo Imaging’s public issue will now go live on October 15 and close on October 19. The defence tech startup’s public issue consists entirely of an offer for sale (OFS) component of up to 1.22 Cr equity shares, with no fresh issue component.

It has also set a price band of ₹665-₹700 per equity share for its ₹852 Cr IPO, which values the company at ₹4,009.8 Cr (about $480 Mn) at the upper end of the spectrum. 

The startup had initially filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI in December last year. It then received SEBI’s approval in July this year. However, the company then re-filed a fresh DRHP in August this year. 

Founded in 2012 by Arvind Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D’Souza, Tonbo Imaging designs and develops advanced imaging and sensor systems for surveillance, reconnaissance and other military applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, handheld thermal imaging binoculars, driver-vision systems, targeting equipment, fire-control systems and missile seekers.

The startup claims that its expertise lies in blending micro-optics, low-power electronics and digital image processing to produce low-power platforms across visible and infrared spectrums.

It counts the likes of NATO, US Navy SEALs, Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), and the defence ministry of Armenia as its customers. At the end of June 2026, the startup claims to have deployed more than 28,000 systems across 24 countries.

On the financial front, Tonbo Imaging reported a net loss of ₹17.7 Cr in Q1 FY27 against an operating revenue of ₹36 Cr. 

For the full fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26), the startup’s revenue from operations declined 22.7% to ₹362.6 Cr from ₹469.1 Cr in FY25. Meanwhile, net profit declined 30% to ₹50.8 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹72.8 Cr in the previous year.
